Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. South Africa Under-19 are seen in a huddle near the ropes and they are joined by the two openers of West Indies Under-19, Adrian Weir and Stephan Pascal. Kwena Maphaka will start the proceedings with the new ball for South Africa Under-19. Let's play...
...  THE RUN CHASE ...

On the other hand, West Indies Under-19 will be disappointed with the fact that they could not capitalise further on the collapse they induced, allowing South Africa Under-19 to post a challenging total. After winning the toss and opting to bowl, made early inroads all thanks to Deshawn James who accounted for the opener Steve Stolk in his second over. Nathan Sealy orchestrated crucial breakthroughs in the middle overs, dismissing set batters Lhuan-dre Pretorius and David Teeger who were looking strong and taking away the game from the West Indies. Sealy emerged as the standout bowler with a pivotal three-wicket haul, complemented by James' two wickets. Will the West Indies unleash an all-out assault in their pursuit of victory, or will the Proteas thwart their efforts, securing their first win? The drama awaits to unfold as the chase comes to you shortly.

Nathan Sealy is in for a chat. He says it was a nice spell but was challenged in the beginning by the left-hander who came hard at him, after which he tried to ball straighter and got the wicket. He then talks about the variation in pace that allowed him to perform well on this track. He further talks about bowling in tandem with Tarrique Edward which has been a nice partnership despite him starting off the radar. Adds that Edward bowled tighter lines and made things easier for him to come back into the groove. He concludes that the total is less than a run a ball and is very confident of getting the job done.

A good fightback with the bat from South Africa Under-19 as they end up with 285 runs on the board! At one stage in the game, this total looked unlikely and they will be pleased with their batting performance. After the early setback, Lhuan-dre Pretorius and David Teeger displayed exceptional batting, steadying the ship and absorbing the pressure. Despite a brief collapse in the middle overs, the skipper Juan James and Dewan Marais initiated a brilliant counter-attack, forming a crucial 131-run partnership for the 7th wicket. Marais notched up his half-century before getting out in the final over but he along with James did not miss out on injecting momentum into South Africa's innings and helped their side post a daunting total.

Oh, no! Needless from the skipper of West Indies Under-19! Nathan Edward lands it on a back of a length, on off, Martin Khumalo gets on his toes and dabs it wide of cover for a single. Stephan Pascal gets to the ball and fires in a throw at the bowling end. He fails to hit and the ball rolls away to wide long on, allowing the batters an extra run. South Africa Under-19 finish on 285/9!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the national anthems and it is now time to set the ball rolling in the Rainbow Nation! The sun is shining in its full glory as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. West Indies Under-19 are in a huddle before they spread out to take their respective field positions. It will be Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Steve Stolk to open the innings for South Africa Under-19. Nathan Sealy will start with the new ball for West Indies Under-19. Off we go...

We are moments away from the first ball in the 15th edition of the Men's Under-19 Cricket World Cup but before that, the match officials and the two teams will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be West Indies' anthem first followed by the national anthem of South Africa.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree is near the deck. He starts by saying that the weather is pleasant and bright and West Indies will like these conditions. He then talks about the dimensions and says that from the University end, it's 73 meters straight, 68 meters to his left and 60 meters on the square right. Lydia Greenway joins him and says they are on pitch 5 and the grass looks nice and tight which means there will be no cracks allowing extra pace for the seamers. She then talks about the diagonal breeze which would allow the left-handers to hit with the breeze.

Juan James, the skipper of South Africa Under-19, says that they would have bowled first as well. Adds that they will look to put up a decent total on the board now. Mentions that it is a proud moment for all of them and not every day you get to play a World Cup at home. Shares that they have spent the last 20 days together and they have the combinations sorted. Further adds that they are looking forward to getting started. States that he has captained before so he is used to the captaincy role.

The captain of West Indies Under-19, Stephan Pascal says that they will bowl first. He says that they have a very balanced bowling attack and will want to get on with them right away. He further talks about the preparations for physical fitness and skills and says they are well-prepared for the tournament. He then concludes that the intensity in these games is what he looks forward to from his side.

The stage is set for the dawn of cricket's next generation as South Africa welcomes the future stars of the sport. The 15th edition of the Men's Under-19 Cricket World Cup is poised to unfold in the Rainbow Nation, featuring 16 teams, with India entering as the defending champions. A double dose of action awaits us on the opening day as the competition hosts, South Africa Under-19, take on the West Indies Under-19  in the inaugural match at the JB Marks Oval in Potchefstroom. England and Scotland are the other two teams present in Group B, which will see the top three teams progress to the Super Six stage. South Africa lifted silverware in 2014, whereas the West Indies were the winners in 2016, as both teams look to get their campaign off to a winning start in search of their second title. In the lead-up to the event, South Africa played warm-up fixtures against Pakistan and Afghanistan, where rain had the final say in both games. Led by all-rounder Juan James, South Africa Under-19 will look to translate their home-soil advantage into success at this World Cup. The onus will be on Steve Stolk and Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who are coming off a good showing with the bat in the recently concluded Under-19 Tri-Nation series between South Africa, India, and Afghanistan. Other than these two, Dewan Marais and David Teeger will also have to come good. Left-arm speedster Kwena Maphaka will spearhead the pace attack for the hosts, and having played in the previous edition of the tournament, he will be looking to bring all his experience into play. Nqobani Mokoena and Martin Khumalo are the other seam bowling options, while Sipho Potsane will handle the spin bowling duties. As for the West Indies Under-19, they breezed past New Zealand in their first warm-up game before the second game against Nepal was washed out. Under the captaincy of right-hand batter Stephan Pascal, the West Indies have shown in the lead-up to the competition that they have what it takes to go all the way. Having made his first-class debut late last year during West Indies A's tour of South Africa, left-hand batter Jordan Johnson will be crucial to their chances in this event. Jewel Andrew is also in good batting form, as is Joshua Dorne for the boys in Maroon. Left-arm spinner Nathan Sealy was the star with the ball in the warm-up fixture against New Zealand and will hold the key in the spin department. As far as their seam attack goes, right-arm medium pacer Isai Thorne will be the leader of the pack, and he will be hoping for support from Nathan Edward and Deshawn James. It promises to be a tightly fought contest between two seemingly evenly-matched teams. Who will get their campaign off to a winning start? We shall find out soon enough.
